name: API-First Development
description: Enforce API contract-first practices, versioning, and documentation standards

rules.name: Public Services Must Have API Contract
rules.description: All public-facing services must have a formal API contract (OpenAPI, gRPC, or GraphQL). The contract is the source of truth and must exist before implementation begins.

config.message: Public-facing service must have an API contract (OpenAPI, gRPC, or GraphQL).

rules.name: API Version Must Be Documented
rules.description: API contracts must include a version identifier. Unversioned APIs make it impossible to manage breaking changes and coordinate consumer migrations.

config.message: API contract must include a version identifier.

rules.name: Breaking Changes Require ADR
rules.description: Any breaking API change must be accompanied by an Architecture Decision Record (ADR) explaining the rationale, migration path, and timeline. This ensures consumers are not blindsided.

config.message: Breaking API change detected. An ADR must document the rationale, impact, and migration plan.

rules.name: Authentication Documented in Contracts
rules.description: All API endpoints must document their authentication requirements in the contract. Consumers need to know auth requirements without reading source code.

config.message: API contract must document authentication requirements for all endpoints.

rules.name: Rate Limiting Specified
rules.description: API contracts for public services must specify rate limiting policies. Without documented limits, consumers cannot build reliable integrations.

config.message: Public API contract must specify rate limiting policies.

rules.name: Standard Error Response Format
rules.description: All API contracts must define error responses using a standard format (RFC 7807 Problem Details or equivalent). Consistent error handling across services reduces consumer integration effort.

config.message: API contract must define error responses using a standard format (e.g., RFC 7807 Problem Details).

rules.name: Internal APIs Must Have Contracts
rules.description: Internal service-to-service APIs should also have contracts, not just public ones. Internal contracts prevent integration drift and enable automated compatibility checking.

config.message: Internal service-to-service API should have a contract to prevent integration drift.

rules.name: Contract Must Match Implementation
rules.description: API contracts must be linked to the implementing container. Unlinked contracts are documentation that drifts from reality.

config.message: API contract must be linked to its implementing container to prevent contract drift.
